source.title: Naturally Computed Scale Invariance in the Residual Stream of ResNet18

record.file_problem: none; full paper and supplementary material are present
record.tranche_reason: The study investigates scale-invariant channels in ResNet18, but does not test neuron-pole interpretability, the stated cross-model shares, or the explanation-scoring claims. Its results concern a different property and behavior.
record.gate_note: The paper reports counts of ResNet18 channels meeting its scale-invariance criteria and ablation effects on ImageNet accuracy under image scaling. These findings are recorded, but they do not measure the versions in the claim. The paper's references to mechanistic interpretability and superposition do not test those claims.
record.test_reason: The study finds and ablates scale-invariant channels in ResNet18. It never measures how many neurons have one main job, how well explanations predict activations, or how canonical polysemantic neurons should be read. Its only mention of superposition is a future-directions remark that more features may be hidden by it. No version of the claim is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors report tentative evidence that the residual stream computes scale invariance in intermediate ResNet18 blocks. Ablating these channels causes disproportionate, though small, accuracy loss under scale transforms, and broader validation is needed.
record.recipe_differences: This study uses feature visualizations and activation criteria to identify scale-invariant ResNet18 channels, then ablates them. It does not use the neuron-explanation methods or measures in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The feature-visualization procedure is stochastic; jitter settings vary by block and layer. The reported ablation effects are measured at scale transformations from 10% through 50%.

fits_no_version.finding: In ResNet18, four blocks contain channels passing feature-visualization scale-invariance criteria: 1.1 (6, ~9.4%), 2.0 (2, ~1.5%), 2.1 (23, ~18%) and 3.1 (46, ~18%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Intermediate ResNet18 residual-stream blocks contain channels with scale-invariant properties, built by summing smaller-scale input and larger-scale pre-sum copies.

fits_no_version.finding: Mean-ablating criteria-passing channels in blocks 2.1 and 3.1 lowers the ratio of scale-ablation to random-ablation accuracy under 10–50% scale transforms, relative to the no-scale ratio. The authors call this effect small but consistent.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Identified scale-invariant channels contribute causally, though modestly, to scale-robust ImageNet classification in ResNet18.

record.peer_reviewed: 2025 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition Workshops (CVPRW)
record.problems: The paper notes that the scale-invariance criteria use feature visualizations rather than a wider range of natural images, and that results may vary because feature visualization is stochastic. The ablation effects are described as small, and the behavioral ablations cover only blocks 2.1 and 3.1. The numerical ratios in Fig. 2 are not stated in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported outcomes were omitted. Fig. 1 and the supplementary visualization grids show examples but do not report additional measured outcome values.

untested.parts: Qwen3-32B neuron-pole job shares; not studied.
Interpretability shares across language models, dense or MoE, and scale; only ResNet18 is studied, and not for interpretability share.
Whether InceptionV1 polysemantic examples detect a shared feature such as pose. Scale-invariant channels are found in ResNet18, but nothing is said about polysemanticity or misreading.

Share of interpretable neurons as a function of tools or architecture. The paper counts scale-invariant channels (about 1.5–18% per block), not interpretable channels, and makes no tool or architecture comparison of interpretability.
Neuron-based attribution graphs versus replacement models; not studied.
Whether activating-example explanations predict held-out firing. The paper notes its criteria rely only on feature visualizations and defers natural-image tests.
Simulation-based automated scoring of neuron explanations; not studied.

record.verdict_notes: The record's relation 'discusses' is changed to 'cites_only': superposition and Olah's circuits work appear only as background or future directions. Rows R5–R14 carry state 'partial' with no version linked. Against the study's own hypothesis, the text reports the effect as consistently present but small, and the values are figure-only. Since they bear on no version, this does not affect any verdict.

versions.untested_parts: Qwen3-32B neuron-pole job shares and whether explanations tested on held-out activations support those shares.
Interpretability shares across language models, dense or MoE architectures, and model scales.
Whether canonical InceptionV1 polysemantic examples detect coherent shared features such as pose.
Interpretability shares in vision models, explanations for messy neurons, and the stated estimates comparing tools or architectures.
Whether attribution graphs built from a large model's own neurons explain behavior without a replacement model and its reconstruction error.
Whether explanations based on activating examples fail to predict held-out activation locations.
Automated scoring of neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Applied two feature-visualization-based criteria to identify channels with scale-invariant properties.
rows.value: six channels (∼ 9.4% of all channels in block)
rows.uncertainty: Results may vary due to the stochastic nature of feature visualization.
rows.note: The criteria compare activations for feature visualizations and scaled images; this is not a measure of whether a neuron has one main job.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Mean-ablated all criteria-passing channels in block 2.1 and compared accuracy ratios with random non-passing-channel ablations; each scale percentage used 10 random-channel trials.
rows.measure: Ratio of top-1 ImageNet validation accuracy for scale-invariant-channel ablation to random-channel ablation
rows.value: figure only; text says scale-transformed ratios were consistently below the no-scale ratio
rows.uncertainty: Standard error across random trials shown in figure
rows.note: The text describes the differences as small but consistent. The figure reports ratios, not an interpretablity or neuron-job measure.
